title: Prepositions
objectives: understand English prepositions and the various ways they connect words
translate the various Greek prepositions and how they relate to the noun inflectional system
be able to recognize and predict when prepositions will elide
identify and translate prepositions when they are compounded with other word forms
master 10 more high frequency vocabulary words

learn.title: Learn English Concepts

content.text: Prepositions are usually small words that link or relate two words together. Often they tell position in space or time.

items.def: Tells of the spatial relationship of the book to the table.
Connects the person's going to the time of the game.

content.text: A [[u]]phrase[[/u]] is a string of closely connected words.  A [[u]]clause[[/u]] is a string of connected words and/or phrases, including both a subject and a verb.
A prepositional phrase is usually composed of a preposition followed by a noun which is called the [[u]]object of the preposition[[/u]]
In English, the object of the preposition is in the objective case. Thus we would say "Send the disk with him" and not "with he" or "with his."
Greek prepositions may be followed by nouns in the genitive, dative, or accusative inflectional forms. Each preposition will have a particular case(s) that it usually goes with.

learn._underline_note: phrase / clause / object of the preposition carry format id 0x62e against a 0x502 body in the run table at 0x2076c; on / after are from the rail walk.

senses: from, because of, by, of (with the genitive)

examples.greek: Ἰησοῦν υἱὸν τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ τὸν ἀπὸ Ναζαρέτ
examples.gloss: Jesus son of Joseph from Nazareth

senses: into, to, among, for, near (with the accusative)
from, out of, of, because of (with the genitive)
in, on, among, when, by, at (with the dative)

examples.greek: ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγει πρὸς Φίλιππον
examples.gloss: he comes to him and said to Philip

senses: through, during, at, by (with the genitive)

examples.greek: διὰ τῶν προφητῶν τῷ υἱῷ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου
examples.gloss: by the prophets about the son of man

senses: according to, to, during (with the accusative)
on, at, in, against (with the dative)

examples.greek: πατὴρ ἐπὶ υἱῷ καὶ υἱὸς ἐπὶ πατρί
examples.gloss: father against son and son against father

content.text: Greek prepositions are connecting or linking words like English prepositions. Each preposition will take a noun in a certain case (genitive, dative, or accusative). This case must be learned along with the preposition's main meaning(s). The most common meanings are listed with each preposition but it is important to observe the context as many other meanings are possible.
Note that the genitive often has the idea of separation, the dative the idea of location, and the accusative motion toward.

Prepositions ending in a vowel often drop the final vowel when it comes before a word that begins with a vowel.
If there is a rough breathing mark on the next word, the consonant may be shifted:
A proclitic is a word that has no accent because it is joined so closely with the accented word that follows it. ἐν, εἰς and ἐκ are proclitics.
They come before (pro) the word with the accent.
Enclitics are accentless words that follow the word with the accent. Personal pronouns are often enclitics.

Prepositions are often found compounded with a verb in Greek. Sometimes the meaning of the compound may be determined by combining the meaning of the preposition with the meaning of the verb. Other times, however, the preposition affects the meaning of the verb in other ways, such as intensifying it.
